pl-l4d39c1-d1e115.summary: Turns to disparity of worship, one of the causes making persons unlawful for marriage.

pl-l4d39c1-d1e118.summary: States that a Christian may not marry a gentile or Jewess, since the Old Testament forbade believers to take unbelieving wives, 'lest they lead your sons after their gods', and Ezra separated Jews' marriages with foreigners; this is kept in the New Testament too.
claims: Marriage with unbelievers is forbidden in both Testaments.

pl-l4d39c1-d1e124.summary: Quotes Augustine: let a woman marry only a man of her religion and a man take only such a wife; the Lord commands it, the Apostle teaches it, both Testaments prescribe it.

pl-l4d39c1-d1e137.summary: Quotes Ambrose: Christian, beware of giving your daughter to a gentile or Jew; beware of taking a Jewish, gentile, or foreign, that is heretical, wife alien to your faith.
claims: Christians must not marry outside the faith, including heretics.

pl-l4d39c1-d1e146.summary: Cites a council: whoever, Christian with Jewess or Jew with Christian, unites carnally is to be wholly separated from the Christian assembly.

pl-l4d39c1-d1e152.summary: Concludes that those of different religion and faith cannot contract marriage.

pl-l4d39c1.summary: Disparity of worship makes persons unlawful for marriage: a Christian may not marry a pagan or Jew, as the Old Testament forbade foreign wives and Ezra separated such marriages, and the New Testament keeps this, as Augustine and Ambrose say; a council separates Christians who unite with Jews from the Christian community. So those of different religion and faith cannot contract marriage.
claims: Disparity of worship is a diriment impediment.
Christians may not marry pagans, Jews, or heretics.
